messages:
vivian: Heads-up — huggingface orgX uploaded a new model bundle. We need artifact provenance and a plan to stage in our registry. Private repo link: https://huggingface.co/orgX/model-beta
andre: I can own the ingest. What exactly is included?
sara: Also need commit SHAs and license info before we copy to staging.
vivian: Artifacts: weights split across 12 shards (model-00001-of-00012.bin ...), config.json, tokenizer files in a separate repo. S3 manifest: s3://hf-exports/orgx/model-beta/2025-04-02/manifest.json
vivian: Manifest fields include: weights_digest: "e3a1b4...f7c9", source_commit: "9a7c1d3" (model repo), tokenizer_commit: "f2e8b4a"
ingest-bot: [automated] No sigstore signatures found on release. Recommend requesting a signed release for production promotion.
andre: Plan: pull blobs and verify sha256 for each shard and for the manifest. If checksums match, push to redwood-models-staging/orgx/model-beta/0.1.0/.
andre: Commands I'll run:
```
aws s3 cp s3://hf-exports/orgx/model-beta/2025-04-02/ ./model-beta --recursive
sha256sum model-beta/model-0000*-of-00012.bin | awk '{print $1}' > local_shard_hashes.txt
python -c "import json; print(json.load(open('model-beta/manifest.json'))['weights_digest'])"
```
sara: For tokenizer: run encode/decode unit tests and compare outputs against HF inference. If mismatch, compute tokenizer fingerprint (sha256 of vocab.json + merges.txt + tokenizer_config.json) and pin it in metadata.
vivian: I ran a quick tokenization check from the tokenizer repo at commit f2e8b4a and got a mismatch on a small sample:
```
HF-API: [154, 17, 25]
Local : [154, 17, 29]
```
Possible off-by-one or different BPE merge table.
jonah: That tokenization drift blocks quantization/quality comparisons — we need exact parity before running perf/4bit experiments. I'll hold qt8/q4 runs until tokenization is nailed down.
sara: Also check vocab size vs config.max_sequence_length and any special token ids. Last mismatch we saw was an offset by 2 in vocab ordering.
andre: I'll compute sha256 for the tokenizer files and add tokenizer_sha256 to registry metadata. Proposed registry path: redwood-models-staging/orgx/model-beta/0.1.0/ with shards/, tokenizer/, manifest.json, and onboarding.json
vivian: Metadata we need to capture (minimal): origin_url, weights_digest, shards_list (filenames), tokenizer_sha256, tokenizer_commit, model_repo_commit, license, sigstore (present/absent), onboarding_notes, owners
jonah: I'll run a smoke gen on fp16 and a small quantization test on a single node once tokenization parity is confirmed. Primary metrics: sample latency, tokens/sec, and a 20-sample quality check.
ingest-bot: [automated] Suggested policy: require either sigstore attestation OR an approved legal waiver before promoting to prod.
emily: (legal) noted, I'm looking at the repo license fields. Tokenizer repo is MIT. Model repo description says "restricted" — need full license blob or CLA. Do not promote to prod until legal confirms commercial compatibility.
vivian: Decision checklist to promote to staging: 1) shard checksums verified; 2) tokenizer fingerprint recorded and parity tests pass; 3) license cleared by legal; 4) smoke generation passes (owners: andre/sara/jonah).
andre: Starting ingest and checksum verification now. ETA ~2h. I'll post local_shard_hashes.txt and manifest digest comparison here.
sara: I'll run tokenizer unit tests and a small perplexity run on a 200-sample eval set. ETA ~4h.
jonah: I'll queue a quick qt8/q4 experiment to run after tokenization parity is confirmed. If parity fails, I'll halt and report diffs.
vivian: Thanks — keep updates in-thread. If legal holds, we'll archive the staging copy under hold/ until cleared. :thumbsup:
